attacksRun.attack: OBL-G16-HARNESS-SPEC is set to leftoverDesign false prematurely, because G16 v2 conditions closure on being accepted AND recorded and no recording exists
attacksRun.evidence: This was the sharpest thing in the file and I pursued it hardest. The cited key is literally named leftoverDesignClosedIfAcceptedAndRecorded, G16 v2 is accepted but unrecorded, D-167 occurs zero times in COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md, and the join still sets the obligation false. What settles it is the repo-wide convention, which is consistent and well evidenced. Sibling joins hold an unauthored harness spec at leftoverDesign true with not-capable-of-riding and the reason 'Naming is not authoring', then flip it to false with qualification-at-named-gate once an independently reviewed specification exists. That transition is recorded across families: component-manifest-leftover-join v1/v2 to v3 for OBL-G15-HARNESS-SPEC, doctor-actor-leftover-join v1/v2 to v3/v4 for OBL-G12 and OBL-G21, and permission-leftover-join v1/v2 to v3/v4 for OBL-G09. Three further joins - lifecycle for G18, packaging for G15 and platform-tcb for G22 - sit at false while citing the same leftoverDesignClosedIfAcceptedAndRecorded key, none of them recorded. The field measures whether design work remains, not whether the register has recorded closure, and the join says so in three places: the reason states 'recording remains a later D-000 act', proposedLaterWork opens 'A later D-000 recording may pin G16 v2. This join does not record D-167', and doesNotCloseLeftoverAlone says the token stays OPEN.

attacksRun.evidence: Nine obligations, each bucketed exactly once across summary's four lists - leftoverDesign, recordedCandidateNotApplied, qualificationAtNamedGate and deferredOrRidesElsewhere - with none duplicated and none omitted. The two obligations with leftoverDesign true are exactly the two carrying not-capable-of-riding standings, and the seven with false carry standings appropriate to their kind: recorded-candidate-not-applied, qualification-at-named-gate twice, and four distinct ride targets. All six summary flags are the values the obligation bodies imply.

observationsNotFindings: The disposition worth the coordinator's attention is OBL-G16-HARNESS-SPEC at leftoverDesign false while G16 v2 remains unrecorded. It is correct by the repository's own consistent convention and the join is transparent that recording is a later D-000 act, but the convention itself has a consequence worth stating plainly: across seven rows there are now harness-spec obligations measured as no longer leftover-design whose specifications carry a single reviewer's ACCEPT and no recording at all. G16 v2 here has Claude ACCEPT 0/0 and no Codex review. The measurement is honest; the thinness of the evidence under it is a property of the convention, not of this artifact.

This join is noticeably finer-grained than its siblings, splitting nine obligations where the distribution and compatibility joins carried seven and five. That granularity is what lets OBL-G16-HARNESS-SPEC go to false without overstating anything, because fixture authoring and CI encodings are carried as their own obligations rather than as unnamed limbs inside it. It is the right shape for a row whose remaining work is genuinely of several different kinds.

Four of the nine obligations are ride-elsewhere dispositions pointing at DR-111, DR-127, DR-118 and G16 itself. None of those target rows is closed, so DR-121's practical remainder is larger than its own two leftover-design entries suggest. The join does not claim otherwise, but a reader taking summary.leftoverDesign as the whole picture would understate what has to happen before DR-121 can be tested.

decision.summaryForCoordinator: No blockers, no should-fix. The one disposition that could have been a blocker is OBL-G16-HARNESS-SPEC at leftoverDesign false: the G16 v2 key it cites is named leftoverDesignClosedIfAcceptedAndRecorded, G16 v2 is accepted but unrecorded, and D-167 appears zero times in COORD. I pursued that hard and it is refuted by the repository's own consistent convention - sibling joins hold an unauthored spec at true with 'Naming is not authoring' and flip it to false with qualification-at-named-gate once an independently reviewed spec exists, a transition recorded in the component-manifest, doctor-actor and permission families, with lifecycle, packaging and platform-tcb all sitting at false while citing the same key and none of them recorded. The field measures remaining design work, not register state, and the join says three times that recording is a later D-000 act it does not perform. Every exact-set claim is exact: namedCorpusNotAuthored is element-wise equal to live G16 v2 and list-equal to namedExecutesLimbs and namedCorpusClasses memberVerbatim, reservedForBlueprintVerbatim equals live v16's six-item reservedForBlueprint, and both v16 rides quotes are byte-exact. All 9 recordedInputs and 6 structured pins recompute with zero mismatches. EE-7e is handled correctly - G16 v2 carries notALiveCellMember true and the join denies both the member slot and execution - and the 'fourth' ordinal, which looked off because the live cell has four members, holds as a denial and matches G16 v2's own definite use of 'the fourth member'. No CI provider or tooling name appears anywhere, no window value appears, QUALIFIED occurs three times as denials, and G13 is kept reserved on DR-118. Two things I flagged without charging: the convention now leaves seven rows with harness-spec obligations measured closed on a single reviewer's ACCEPT and no recording, and four of this row's nine obligations ride target rows that are themselves open, so DR-121's practical remainder is larger than its two leftover-design entries suggest. 20 attacks run, 20 refuted.
